title: Structs
bridge: C has no classes, but a `struct` bundles related fields: `struct Reading { int hour; double temp; };`. Access fields with `.` (`r.temp`), or `->` through a pointer (`p->temp`). Functions that work on a struct take it (or a pointer to it) as a parameter. It's a class without methods or private parts.

exercises.title: Hottest hour
exercises.prompt: With the Reading struct given, write int hottest_hour(const Reading log[], int n) (n is at least 1): the hour of the highest temperature (the earliest one on a tie).

tests.hint_if_fail: On a tie keep the earliest: only switch on strictly hotter.

hints: Keep the index of the best so far.

exercises.title: Tank state
exercises.prompt: Write void tank_add(Tank *t, double litres) for the Tank struct given: add litres to t->level, but never above t->capacity or below 0 (negative litres means water used).
hints: if (t->level > t->capacity) t->level = t->capacity; if (t->level < 0) t->level = 0;

quiz.q: Access a field through a pointer p?

choices: Gives the struct type a short name
quiz.why: So you can write Reading instead of struct Reading.

quiz.q: Can a struct have methods in C?
choices: No: you write functions that take the struct

explain: Explain structs to someone who has never programmed, in your own words, with an example you make up.
